learningObjective: Diagnose why a measured GEMM throughput falls significantly below the theoretical peak and identify the most plausible cause.

canonicalClaims.claim: For a large square GEMM with AI far above the ridge point, achieved throughput below peak is typically explained by imperfect Tensor Core packing (prologue/epilogue, tile boundaries, MMA scheduling) rather than by memory or launch overhead, and is consistent with a Tensor Core utilization metric well below 100%.
conditions: Profile shows HBM not saturated (so not memory-bound).
Kernel runtime is not so short that launch overhead dominates.
nonImplications: Does not imply Tensor Core utilization percentage maps linearly to achieved TFLOP/s across all metrics.
Does not imply the gap is unfixable; larger tiles, better scheduling, and vendor-tuned kernels can close some of it.

misconceptions.claim: A GEMM falling below peak must be memory-bound.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Being below peak has many causes; Roofline says memory-bound only when AI < ridge. Profile evidence of HBM saturation is required to attribute the gap to memory.

misconceptions.claim: Kernel launch overhead can account for a 30% gap on a multi-millisecond GEMM.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Launch overhead is microseconds; large GEMMs run many milliseconds, so launch overhead is a negligible fraction.

misconceptions.claim: GEMMs at the ridge point achieve peak throughput.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Ridge is a theoretical crossover; achieving peak requires efficient tiling, high occupancy, and full MMA pipeline packing regardless of ridge alignment.

implementationFacts: AI for N^3 GEMM: N/3 FLOP/byte for FP16.
A100 FP16 ridge ~ 156 FLOP/byte; N=8192 GEMM is deeply compute-bound.
Nsight Compute Tensor Core Active metric ≈ fraction of SM cycles with Tensor Core issuing.
performanceScenarios: Vendor-tuned cuBLAS reaches ~ 75–85% of peak on square GEMMs; further gains come from problem-specific kernels (CUTLASS, hand-tuned).
